subject.title: fix: models status auth, browser local-file nav, codex workspace app-server, tui empty sessions

question: Should Codex app-server workspace-write turns gain network access by default, or should network egress remain denied unless a maintainer-approved opt-in path is added?
rationale: This changes a sandbox/security boundary for existing users, and automation cannot decide whether the product should trade default isolation for app-server connectivity.

options.title: Keep default-denied and repair the PR
options.body: Preserve networkAccess false for workspace-write, add any network-enabled path as an explicit maintainer-approved opt-in, and keep the narrower browser/auth/TUI fixes reviewable.

options.title: Approve network-enabled workspace-write
options.body: Maintainers may intentionally accept networkAccess true by default, but the PR should add matching docs, upgrade/security rationale, and real behavior proof.

options.title: Split the security-boundary change
options.body: Land only the narrower TUI/browser/auth fixes once repaired and proven, and move the sandbox default decision to a separate maintainer-owned item.

recommendation.title: Keep default-denied and repair the PR
recommendation.body: Preserve networkAccess false for workspace-write, add any network-enabled path as an explicit maintainer-approved opt-in, and keep the narrower browser/auth/TUI fixes reviewable.

likelyOwner.reason: The current-main blame and related auth/browser/sandbox history point to steipete as the best available reviewer for this security-boundary decision.
